children: Palantir Technologies Inc. Class A (NASDAQ:PLTR) topped Q2 with $1.94B revenue, huge cash flow and raised 2026 guidance while winning an Army TITAN contract and hiring Peter Zaffino for financial services, even as investor Michael Burry and Gemini 3.8 Flash competition pose growth and valuation risks.
Palantir Q2 Revenue Growth Guidance Raised
: Palantir (PLTR) Q2 revenue $1.94B, up 93% YoY; U.S. commercial sales $764M (+149%); adjusted free cash flow $1.22B; raised 2026 revenue guidance to $8.15–8.16B.
: Palantir (PLTR) won an Army prime contract to deliver eight TITAN ground stations (4 Advanced, 4 Basic), handling manufacture, delivery, software, subsystem integration and fielding for the Army.
: Investor Michael Burry warned Palantir (PLTR) could drop from a roughly $432B market cap to under $100B, citing weak fundamentals and software-style pricing—key risks for traders.
: Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash Cyber launch cited as a potential competitive headwind for Palantir (PLTR) government business, raising investor concern about near-term growth prospects.

: Palantir (PLTR) hired Peter Zaffino as Global Head of Financial Services, effective Jan 15, 2027, to lead growth across insurance, banking, asset management, private equity and other finance clients.
